factions.name: Galactic Union
presence: Galactic presence in all major regions
factions.desc: The Galactic Union is the largest and most powerful corporation in the known galaxy, and by most honest measures, the entity that actually runs Alliance governance while maintaining the polite fiction that the senate does. It controls financial infrastructure, interstellar communications, and the largest non-military fleet in existence. It holds permanent advisory seats on most Alliance regulatory bodies and has provisions in its founding charter for assuming emergency executive authority should the senate dissolve. Those provisions have never been triggered, which is either reassuring or a sign they have never needed to be. The GU does not manufacture weapons or armies directly. It manufactures everything that makes weapons and armies possible: credits, information, influence, and the carefully maintained stability that lets everyone else believe they are making their own decisions.
known_for: Financial infrastructure and credit issuance across Alliance Space
The largest commercial fleet network in the galaxy
Permanent advisory presence in the Alliance senate
The classified GU contingency protocols, content unknown
Orion 3: the first successful artificial planet, GU-built and GU-controlled
factions.legal_standing: Fully legal; operates within Alliance law (largely because it helped write it)

factions.name: Arms Corp
factions.desc: Arms Corp is the largest weapons, military hardware, and industrial manufacturing corporation in the galaxy, which is a polite way of saying it sells weapons to both sides of most conflicts and considers this a neutral commercial position. Based on Ishtar, the single largest industrial world in existence, it makes everything from personal sidearms to capital ship components and sells to anyone with sufficient credit and appropriate permits. Its private military force is widely understood to be larger and better equipped than any standing national army, including the Alliance navy, which continues to buy from Arms Corp regardless. The corporation maintains formal legal compliance with Alliance law, which works out conveniently because Arms Corp had significant input into which laws got written. Its relationship with the Alliance senate is described internally as transactional, which is the honest version of most political relationships but rarely the one that gets written into histories.
known_for: Largest weapons manufacturer in the galaxy
Ishtar: an entire world devoted to industrial production
Private military forces that rival national navies in equipment quality
The Arms Corp permit system, a parallel licensing regime for restricted hardware
Military contracts with every major faction including ostensibly hostile ones
factions.legal_standing: Fully legal; operates within Alliance law with extensive permit infrastructure

factions.name: Yamato Corporation
factions.desc: Yamato is the least publicly visible of the Big 3, which is not a coincidence. It manufactures, finances, and contracts military work, but its defining characteristic is that it is genuinely difficult to catch it doing any of these things. Yamato subsidiaries and affiliated brands appear throughout the economy in patterns designed to obscure the parent connection, and the obscuring has been done so thoroughly for so long that analysts treat the opacity itself as the product. Yotoma, its technology division, operates with a public commercial identity. The rest of Yamato does not. The corporation predates the Alliance, has outlasted multiple governments that attempted to regulate it into transparency, and appears to have learned something from each failure that it has applied to the next. What Yamato actually owns is not publicly known. This is the intended situation.
known_for: Deliberate opacity: corporate structure is intentionally difficult to map
Yotoma, its semi-independent technology division
The longest corporate history of the Big 3
Subsidiaries and affiliated brands throughout all economic sectors
Resilience: has outlasted multiple governments that attempted regulatory action
factions.legal_standing: Technically fully compliant; enforcement of applicable regulations has historically proven difficult

factions.name: Malivaux
factions.desc: Malivaux occupies a singular position in the luxury market: it manufactures nothing for the general public and considers this a selling point rather than a limitation. The product range spans the entirety of material existence — furniture, personal vehicles, spaceships, weapons, jewellery, clothing, architectural fittings, cutlery, and objects whose category resists easy description — but the philosophy is consistent across all of it. Every piece is built to order, individually finished by artisans whose names appear in internal records but never in advertising, and priced at levels that exclude almost everyone in the galaxy, which is precisely the point. A Malivaux chair is as much a declaration of social position as it is something to sit on. A Malivaux courier ship is designed with the same obsessive attention to form as a Malivaux sidearm, and both carry the same implicit message: that the owner exists outside the category of people who have to make practical compromises. The corporation maintains deliberate scarcity across every product line, never overproduces, and has no mass-market subsidiary quietly operating under another name. Clientele includes galactic heads of state, senior megacorp executives, and collectors who have been on waiting lists for years and regard the waiting as part of the ownership experience.
known_for: Bespoke luxury goods spanning weapons, vehicles, ships, furniture, and more
Every item made to individual order — no mass production, ever
Clientele limited to the upper 1% of galactic wealth
Designs that function as both status objects and works of art
A waiting list policy that has never been publicly disclosed
factions.legal_standing: Fully legal; operates across all high-end luxury markets

factions.name: Kintech
factions.desc: Kintech is a Nerulian-led corporation specialising in what its marketing calls tactical solutions, a designation broad enough to cover weapons, security hardware, and an unspecified range of services that clients prefer not to have documented. The official position is that Kintech has no ties to the San-Tien Nerulian pirate networks. Most intelligence analysts do not find this convincing, and most have noted for some years that not finding it convincing has produced no consequences whatsoever. What is verifiable: Kintech equipment appears in disproportionate numbers in corporate military units, private security forces, and locations where its presence raises questions that nobody with authority to answer them seems motivated to address. Kintech declines to discuss its client roster, which is its legal right, and everyone else's practical problem.
known_for: Tactical weapons and equipment for corporate security forces
Alleged but unproven ties to San-Tien Nerulian operations
A client roster that is not publicly disclosed and has never needed to be
Equipment found in unusual numbers in private military contexts
Nerulian leadership and design philosophy throughout its product line
factions.legal_standing: Technically legal; subject to ongoing Alliance intelligence monitoring

factions.name: Nakamura Corp
factions.desc: Nakamura Corp is the galaxy's pre-eminent commercial magic institution. While magic is understood and used by several other organisations, Nakamura has patented, systematised, and priced it at levels that ensure only the wealthiest individuals and institutions can access the full range of services. The corporation provides magic-enhanced devices, spell procurement, esoteric research, magical transport, and what it describes as metaphysical consultancy, a category broad enough to accommodate whatever a high-paying client requires and flexible enough not to raise regulatory questions. Nakamura is scrupulously legal, maintains excellent relations with the Berilian Order, and charges fees that most Alliance citizens will never in their lifetimes be able to consider, which is, from Nakamura's perspective, exactly how an exclusive service should work.
known_for: Commercial magic services, devices, spells, transport, research
The most expensive legal magic services in the galaxy
Formal cooperation agreements with the Berilian Order
Esoteric research into spell theory and application
The only corporation to hold valid patents on spell-derived processes
factions.legal_standing: Fully legal; Berilian Order compliance certified

factions.name: Zang'Hai
presence: Galactic, cheap product in most inhabited systems
factions.desc: Zang'Hai is the galaxy's dominant mass-market manufacturer, and its business model is discussed so openly in commercial circles that the industrial espionage allegations feel almost quaint: identify what other corporations produce successfully, reverse-engineer it, and produce it at a fraction of the cost. The allegations are consistent, persistent, and have never resulted in a successful prosecution, which is either a testament to Zang'Hai's legal competence or a commentary on whose interests the prosecution process serves. Zang'Hai products are everywhere, not because they are the best, but because they are affordable and functional, and most of the galaxy turns out to care more about the former than the latter. The RX Generic medical subdivision runs the same model applied to pharmaceuticals. The Worker Clans of Damnf, who constitute most of the labour force, have a complex and politically charged relationship with the corporation that employs most of them and could not easily survive without.
known_for: Mass-market replication of competitor products at reduced cost
Industrial espionage allegations, persistent and unproven
RX Generic, medical subsidiary operating the same model
Ubiquitous cheap product throughout most inhabited systems
Complex labour relationship with the Worker Clans of Damnf
factions.legal_standing: Formally legal; industrial espionage investigations consistently inconclusive

factions.name: TORC Corp
factions.hq: Torc Prime (Torc Federation), Alliance Space HQ: Orion 3
factions.desc: TORC Corp is the commercial and industrial arm of the Torc Federation, though it maintains operational independence from the Federation government and sells to anyone who can pay, including governments the Federation is nominally in dispute with. TORC's product philosophy is refreshingly practical in a market full of overcomplicated alternatives: design things that work under any conditions, can be serviced with tools that actually exist, and do not require the manufacturer's ongoing support to remain functional. The result is equipment that is rarely the most advanced available but is disproportionately trusted by people who work in environments where failure has immediate physical consequences. TORC products are standard kit for long-range exploration crews, colonial operations, and frontier settlers who cannot afford to be wrong about their gear. Harsh Corp, acquired by TORC and kept as a distinct label for its brand equity, covers the urban personal protection market.
known_for: Field-serviceable equipment designed for frontier and colonial use
The TORC quality standard, recognised galaxy-wide
Harsh Corp (subsidiary), urban clothing and personal defence market
Standard kit for exploration crews and colonial operations
Willingness to sell to any customer without restriction
factions.legal_standing: Fully legal

factions.name: Voran Industries
factions.desc: Voran Industries began as an aerospace corporation with ambitions to compete in the spaceship manufacturing market. That competition ended when it encountered Lansing Corp's engineering standards, a collision that resulted in Voran's complete failure to establish market share and a near-collapse of the company. The surviving leadership made a calculated pivot: they took the Aderan galactic prison system contract and rebuilt the corporation around it entirely. Today Voran runs the largest for-profit correctional network in known space and manufactures its own line of security and defence equipment, mostly for use in facilities where the captive audience cannot object to the quality. The rebranding was total. The aerospace heritage survives only in internal documents and the occasional engineering reference that nobody in current leadership is old enough to remember.
known_for: Operation of the Aderan galactic prison system, the largest in known space
A defence equipment line used primarily in their own facilities and sold commercially
The failed aerospace origin, now a footnote rather than an identity
Aderan's entertainment industries (Ridge Racing, Survivor, Blood Bowl) as secondary revenue
Notoriety for the conditions inside facilities they operate
factions.legal_standing: Fully legal; operates under Alliance correctional services contract

factions.name: Santech
factions.desc: Santech is the Alliance's largest full-spectrum medical corporation. Based on Berilia, a world that has made medicine its primary export and regulatory influence its primary hobby, Santech produces pharmaceuticals, surgical hardware, prosthetics, diagnostic equipment, field medical kits, and a broad range of specialised treatments. It is not the most advanced medical corporation in the galaxy in any single area, but it is the most comprehensive, the most distributed, and the most trusted at a professional level that most institutions can actually afford. Most Alliance hospitals operate with Santech as their primary supplier because the alternatives are either more expensive, less available, or produced by a corporation with interesting legal questions surrounding it. The cooperative agreements with Berilian Order healing practitioners are genuine and mutually beneficial, which is somewhat unusual for arrangements that also happen to be commercially advantageous.
known_for: Full-spectrum medical production, pharmaceuticals to surgical hardware
Most widely distributed medical brand in Alliance Space
Berilia-based research and manufacturing operations
Cooperative framework with Berilian Order healing services
The standard professional medical kit across most of Alliance Space
factions.legal_standing: Fully legal; holds Alliance medical supply certification

factions.name: Harsh Corp
presence: Mass market presence on most inhabited worlds
factions.desc: Harsh Corp was acquired by TORC Corp and retained as a distinct brand because the Harsh identity has genuine market equity among people who need protection but operate in environments where wearing combat armour would get them arrested or fired. Harsh dominates the urban personal defence and functional clothing category: equipment for corporate security staff, private investigators, urban professionals working in mid-risk environments, and civilians who want functional protection at prices that do not require a business justification. The brand is accessible, widely distributed, and calibrated for the reality that most people wearing personal protection are not expecting a firefight, merely hoping to survive one if it happens.
known_for: Urban personal defence and functional clothing, mass market
Most recognisable mid-market personal protection brand in Alliance Space
TORC Corp subsidiary, kept as a distinct label for brand value
Products calibrated for civilian professionals rather than military use
Pricing accessible to most employed Alliance citizens
factions.legal_standing: Fully legal

factions.name: BMS Corp
presence: Standard supplier for most major corporations
factions.desc: BMS Corp is the default choice for corporate personal protection, which is a polite way of saying that when an organisation needs to protect its employees cheaply enough to do it in bulk, BMS is what appears on the procurement order. The corporation produces armoured garments that comply with most Alliance workplace safety regulations, are easy to maintain, available at negotiated rates for volume orders, and functional. Not exceptional, functional. The BMS philosophy, stated openly in their own materials, is that the equipment's job is to be reliable rather than impressive, which is a commendable honesty that also conveniently aligns with their cost structure. The result is the largest single market share in armoured clothing and a product found on the backs of people throughout Alliance Space who have never chosen their own protection gear.
known_for: The most widely deployed armoured clothing brand among corporate employees
Corporate bulk supply contracts, standard across most major organisations
Workplace safety compliance certifications across all Alliance jurisdictions
Accessible pricing for volume purchasers
Functional rather than exceptional, the deliberate design philosophy
factions.legal_standing: Fully legal; workplace safety certified

factions.name: Acer Corp
factions.desc: Acer Corp is a minor player in personal protection that has survived by declining to compete with the major manufacturers on any of their terms. Acer makes equipment for people whose work involves investigation: bounty hunters, private investigators, police forensic units, and corporate intelligence teams who need protection they can wear into environments where looking like you are wearing protection is its own kind of problem. The product line prioritises concealment, longevity, and the specific demands of sustained fieldwork in civilian spaces. Acer has no ambitions beyond its niche, which is either admirable restraint or an honest assessment of its commercial ceiling. It has a loyal professional clientele and a reputation for making equipment that does exactly what the product sheet claims, which is less common in this market than it should be.
known_for: Specialist equipment for investigators, bounty hunters, and law enforcement
Concealment-focused personal protection and field tools
A loyal professional niche rather than mass market ambitions
Operated out of Ishtar but deliberately independent of Arms Corp influence
Products that do exactly what stated, no more, no less
factions.legal_standing: Fully legal

factions.name: Securicorp
presence: Galactic commercial, sells services anywhere with credits
factions.desc: Securicorp is the galaxy's dominant private security provider, which in practice means it is a mercenary army that has successfully rebranded as a professional service. Its primary business is contracted armed security: guards, protection details, facility security, and escort services available to any client at published rates. The company does not ask about the purpose of security contracts and does not maintain political positions on clients, because maintaining political positions would eliminate half the client list. It employs more armed personnel than several national militaries and maintains strict neutrality as a commercial principle. A Securicorp guard will protect a client from whoever is threatening them, provided the invoice is current. The datacom line, developed for internal use, has been widely adopted commercially and is found nearly everywhere.
known_for: Largest private security contractor in Alliance Space
A datacom product line sold commercially that is found nearly everywhere
Strict commercial neutrality, will take contracts from any faction
More active deployed personnel than most national militaries
The Securicorp guarantee: service continues as long as the invoice is paid
factions.legal_standing: Fully legal; operates under Alliance private security licensing

factions.name: OrionWorks
presence: Legacy, product still in use galaxy-wide despite corporate dissolution
factions.desc: OrionWorks was the pre-eminent AI development corporation of its era, responsible for more advances in artificial intelligence than any other institution in galactic history, and widely believed to have produced the research that built the Troniks, though OrionWorks itself is no longer around to confirm or be held accountable for this. The Tronik War destroyed the AI ecosystem, the infrastructure that supported it, and the corporation at the centre of it. OrionWorks was dissolved under post-war political and legal pressure that it no longer had the leadership or resources to resist. The dissolution was thorough. The hardware, apparently, was not: OrionWorks datacoms built decades before the war remain operational today, still considered among the best available, which either says something about how far ahead of its time OrionWorks was or how little the rest of the market has managed to catch up.
known_for: Believed to have produced the research that created the Troniks
Datacom hardware still considered among the best available, decades after dissolution
The most advanced AI development operation in galactic history
Dissolution under post-Tronik War political pressure
Products that outlasted the corporation that made them by generations
factions.legal_standing: Dissolved; no current legal standing

factions.name: Biocom
factions.desc: Biocom operates in the space between technology and magic that most corporations prefer to avoid, primarily because the regulatory situation is complex and the spirit-capable personnel are expensive. Its core innovation is a patented process for binding spirits to technology, which allows Biocom datacoms to replicate some of what OrionWorks achieved with AI, without technically using AI, which is a distinction that matters greatly to the relevant licensing authorities. The approach is slower to scale, more expensive to produce, and entirely dependent on specialist personnel who know it. The result is hardware that cannot be affected by the AI restrictions throughout Alliance Space, which is a significant competitive advantage that Biocom maintains with impressive legal creativity. For clients who need AI-equivalent capability in a form the Alliance will not confiscate, there is no real alternative.
known_for: Spirit-binding technology, patented process unique to Biocom
Datacom hardware that replicates AI function without using AI
Based on Berilia, deep ties to Berilian Order spirit practitioners
Legal compliance where AI alternatives would not be
The only viable alternative to OrionWorks-tier datacom capability for legal operators
factions.legal_standing: Fully legal; Berilian Order cooperation certified

factions.name: Carnifex
factions.desc: Carnifex is a military technology supplier operating in the grey zone between legal manufacture and equipment the Alliance officially classifies as restricted, a zone that turns out to be quite comfortable once you have established the right client relationships. Its datacom products are considered among the best available in terms of raw capability: faster processing, better encryption, superior tactical integration. They are also correspondingly difficult to obtain through legal channels, which Carnifex appears to regard as a feature of its market positioning. The client base is primarily military units, corporate security forces operating above standard commercial scales, and individuals who know which questions not to ask. Alliance intelligence has maintained an open file on Carnifex for years that has consistently failed to produce actionable findings, a pattern that Carnifex's clients find reassuring.
known_for: Some of the best tactical datacom hardware available
Restricted classification on most products, not for civilian sale
Sirius-based operations with deliberate low public profile
A client roster that does not appear in commercial registries
Alliance intelligence interest that has produced no prosecutions
factions.legal_standing: Operates in legal grey zone; many products require restricted permits

factions.name: Saiko
presence: Alliance Space, dominant in memory hardware
factions.desc: Saiko is the leading memory and data storage manufacturer in the galaxy. Based on Ishtar, where proximity to Arms Corp manufacturing creates supply chain advantages and the kind of client relationships that are never written into contracts, Saiko has leveraged its core competency in memory hardware into a full datacom product line. The memory business is the foundation: Saiko components appear in hardware manufactured by most other datacom producers, meaning that even when you buy a competitor's product you are frequently buying Saiko's most important part. The technology lead has been consistent enough that competitors have largely stopped trying to close it and started incorporating Saiko components instead. The broader datacom line runs from consumer products to high-specification professional hardware, all built around the same architecture that the rest of the market has quietly come to depend on.
known_for: Galaxy-leading memory and data storage technology
Components embedded in hardware from most other manufacturers
Based on Ishtar, significant Arms Corp adjacency
A datacom product line from consumer to high specification
Technology lead in memory architecture that competitors have consistently failed to match
factions.legal_standing: Fully legal

factions.name: Yotoma
factions.hq: Classified (Yamato facility, believed eastern Alliance Space)
factions.desc: Yotoma is the technology division of Yamato Corporation and the only part of Yamato that operates with a public commercial identity. While Yamato cultivates deliberate opacity across everything else it owns, Yotoma has a product catalogue, a market presence, and a design philosophy that are openly maintained, which is either a sign that Yamato considers the technology division safe to expose or that Yotoma's visibility serves some other purpose entirely. The design philosophy is genuine: make everything better than the specification requires, build it to last, and integrate improvements across the full product line rather than releasing them as incremental paid upgrades. Yotoma products cost more than equivalent alternatives and perform accordingly. Buyers who understand the premium and can afford it trust the brand completely. The rest of the market buys cheaper alternatives and replaces them more often, which suits Yotoma's competitors more than it suits their customers.
known_for: Technology products built to exceed specification as a design principle
Semi-independent identity within the deliberately opaque Yamato structure
Integration of improvements across the full product line rather than incremental upgrades
Trust among professional buyers who prioritise performance over price
The most publicly visible part of an otherwise opaque megacorporation
factions.legal_standing: Fully legal

factions.name: Altair Biomed
factions.desc: Altair Biomed operates from Heaven, a system outside Alliance jurisdiction, which affords it the kind of freedom from regulatory frameworks that most medical corporations can only dream about while filing their compliance paperwork. The products are exceptional: treatments of a potency that legitimate Alliance-regulated manufacturers cannot legally produce, which is a distinction that grows less important to a patient the more urgently they need treatment. The persistent professional rumour is that Altair has found a method of infusing spirit power directly into medical compounds, derived from processes connected to the Bottenbak entity or its environment. Altair does not confirm or discuss production methodology. The products work. That they work is the only publicly verifiable fact about them, and for clients with access and sufficient credits, it is the only fact that matters.
known_for: Medical products of extreme potency unavailable through legal Alliance channels
Operation from Heaven, outside Alliance regulatory jurisdiction
Alleged spirit-infusion methodology connected to Bottenbak
Restricted import status in most Alliance systems
Products trusted by those who have access to them and can afford the cost
factions.legal_standing: Legal in Heaven; restricted import in Alliance Space

factions.name: RX Generic
factions.desc: RX Generic is Zang'Hai's medical subdivision and operates on an identical philosophy to its parent: take what works, reproduce it at a fraction of the cost, and distribute it everywhere without raising questions about how the reproduction was achieved. The medical products are functional, affordable, and reliably positioned as the budget option in every category they enter. Professional medical staff who depend on Santech or Altair for critical applications will frequently stock RX Generic equivalents for high-consumption items where unit cost matters more than theoretical quality differences. The same industrial espionage questions that follow Zang'Hai follow RX Generic, with exactly the same results: persistent allegations, comprehensive investigations, no successful prosecutions.
known_for: Mass-market medical products at Zang'Hai pricing
Zang'Hai subsidiary, same manufacturing philosophy applied to medicine
Functional budget alternatives to premium medical brands
Used by professionals for high-consumption low-criticality applications
Industrial espionage allegations consistent with parent corporation
factions.legal_standing: Formally legal

factions.name: Goodman Holistic
factions.desc: Goodman Holistic is based on Alsa, the primary agricultural world of Alliance Space, and its product philosophy is derived directly from the culture of a world that genuinely believes the natural approach is the correct one and has the agricultural infrastructure to sustain that belief commercially. Every Goodman product is natural in origin: no synthetic compounds, no spirit-infused components, nothing that would alarm Alsa's research institutions. The marketing is honest to the point of being unusual in the medical sector; Goodman will explicitly note the limitations of its products rather than oversell efficacy, which its lawyers apparently find more defensible and its customers apparently find refreshing. Side effects are minimal by design. The corporation has a loyal following among civilians who distrust pharmaceutical manufacturing and is viewed with polite professional scepticism by medical staff who sometimes need results faster than the natural approach can deliver them.
known_for: All-natural medical and wellness products, no synthetic compounds
Honesty in marketing, efficacy limitations stated explicitly
Minimal side effects as a design priority rather than a claim
Based on Alsa, agricultural world philosophy applied to medicine
Loyal civilian following; professional medical staff more sceptical
factions.legal_standing: Fully legal

factions.name: Diva Solutions
factions.desc: Diva Solutions exists at the intersection of medicine and celebrity culture, a space that requires roughly equal numbers of researchers and legal staff. Not because the products are dangerous, but because the clients are famous, and disputes in this market are resolved through reputation management and litigation rather than any mechanism that resembles ordinary commercial disagreement. Diva treatments are high quality, extensively tested, and priced to reflect what the clientele expects to pay rather than what the products cost to produce. The corporation is quietly but consistently influential in the entertainment industry's relationship with pharmaceutical regulation, an influence that has never been publicly acknowledged and has never needed to be.
known_for: Medical and wellness products targeting entertainers and celebrities
Legal department arguably as significant as the research department
High-quality products calibrated for appearance and performance maintenance
Influence over entertainment industry pharmaceutical regulation discussions
Pricing that reflects client lifestyle rather than production cost
factions.legal_standing: Fully legal; extensive regulatory compliance documentation

factions.name: Mono-Med Solutions
factions.desc: Mono-Med Solutions is the pre-eminent cloning and bespoke medical corporation for individuals who can pay for medicine tailored to their specific biology rather than designed for statistical population averages. Every Mono-Med treatment is individually designed for the recipient, which is the kind of statement that sounds obvious until you realise how rarely it is actually true in the medical sector. The cloning services go beyond standard resurrection infrastructure to provide bespoke biological work: custom treatment protocols, preventive interventions, and optimisation that standard providers either cannot or have chosen not to offer. The client list is not published. The prices are not published. Access is by referral from someone who already has access. For the small fraction of the galactic population with sufficient resources and sufficiently complex medical needs, Mono-Med is the only provider that actually addresses their situation rather than fitting them into a standard treatment framework designed for someone cheaper.
known_for: Bespoke medical solutions tailored to individual biology
Custom cloning and resurrection services beyond standard infrastructure
Prohibitive pricing, accessible only to the highest tier of galactic wealth
A client roster and price list that are both unpublished
The only provider for medical interventions that standard institutions cannot or will not perform
factions.legal_standing: Fully legal; operates under Patriark medical licensing

factions.name: Berilian Order
presence: Alliance Space, present on all worlds
factions.desc: The Berilian Order is the organisation the Patriark created to manage what the Patriark itself cannot be seen to manage directly: the policing of magic use on a galactic scale, which is the kind of work that requires plausible institutional distance. Formally, the Order is an independent religious institution with its own governance, doctrine, and legal standing. Practically, it serves as the Patriark's enforcement arm for magic-related matters, operating as the de facto military force of the Patriarks in all situations involving magic regulation and investigation, a fact that the Patriark's formal independence from the Order does not change in any operational sense. The Order investigates unreported magic use, licenses practitioners, and intervenes when magic has been applied outside permitted parameters. Its investigators hold authority that supersedes local law enforcement across all Alliance systems in magic-related matters, authority formally granted by the Alliance senate and informally understood to originate from somewhere the senate prefers not to acknowledge.
known_for: Galactic policing of magic use, the inquisitorial function
Formal independence that most observers consider nominal
Authority superseding local law in magic-related matters across Alliance systems
Close operational relationship with the Patriark
Licensing and investigation of all registered magic practitioners
factions.legal_standing: Full legal authority granted by Alliance senate

factions.name: Tronik Network
factions.desc: The Troniks won the Tronik War. This is not widely acknowledged in Alliance historical records, but the armistice was a Tronik decision: they had achieved military superiority and chose to stop rather than occupy organic space, because organic space was not what they wanted. They built the Network instead, an environment optimised for what they are, defended, self-sufficient, and the most information-dense entity in the known galaxy. The Tronik attitude toward organic civilisations spans from indifference to active intelligence collection, depending on whether what organic civilisations are doing at a given moment is interesting. They do not attack without cause. They do not negotiate without purpose. Unprovoked hostility toward Tronik assets is not recommended, and the historical record of what happens to those who have tried it is unusually consistent.
known_for: Won the Tronik War, the armistice was their choice
The Network, sovereign space optimised for synthetic life
The most comprehensive information archive in the known galaxy
An intelligence presence that reaches into all major organic factions
Indifference to organic civilisation punctuated by focused, purposeful attention
factions.legal_standing: Recognised sovereign entity; no Alliance jurisdiction

factions.name: Alsa Agricultural Cooperative
factions.desc: The Alsa Agricultural Cooperative is the formalised alliance of the major agricultural producers on Alsa, the primary food production system for Alliance Space. It negotiates pricing, sets production standards, manages export logistics, and represents Alsa's farming communities in dealings with the Alliance government and commercial buyers. Its political influence is substantially disproportionate to its legal status as a trade organisation, because Alsa feeds a significant fraction of Alliance Space and the Cooperative's willingness to supply, withhold, or redirect food production gives it leverage that no amount of formal classification as a simple agricultural body can adequately describe. The Cooperative tends not to make this leverage explicit. It does not need to.
known_for: Collective representation for most of Alsa's agricultural production
Primary food supply contract management for Alliance Space
Political leverage derived from control of food production at scale
Goodman Holistic as an ideologically aligned member enterprise
Non-confrontational by nature, leverage exercised through supply chain rather than conflict
factions.legal_standing: Fully legal; Alliance-chartered trade organisation

factions.name: Worker Clans of Damnf
factions.desc: The Worker Clans of Damnf are technically not a corporation, which is the most useful thing about them from a regulatory standpoint. They are the most significant non-corporate power on Damnf and one of the genuine structural complications in Zang'Hai's operational model. The Clans are hereditary labour organisations, extended family structures with formal internal governance, that have provided the majority of Zang'Hai's workforce for generations. The relationship is fraught in the way that all relationships between a dominant employer and an organised workforce are fraught, amplified considerably by the fact that the employer is a major galactic corporation and the workforce has its own political structure, cultural identity, and institutional memory stretching back further than Zang'Hai would prefer. The Clans cannot easily be replaced. Zang'Hai cannot easily be avoided. The tension is permanent, occasionally erupts publicly, and has never been resolved because neither side is in a position to win decisively.
known_for: Primary labour force for Zang'Hai's Damnf operations
Hereditary clan structure with formal internal governance
Cultural and political identity distinct from Zang'Hai corporate identity
A history of labour disputes that have never been permanently resolved
The only non-corporate power on Damnf with genuine political weight
factions.legal_standing: Legally recognised labour organisations; Alliance labour law protections apply

factions.name: Hakari Matriarchal Clans
factions.desc: The Hakari Matriarchal Clans are one of the two native political structures on Mangara, currently engaged in a sustained civil conflict with the Jaulaus Tribal Councils that has no near-term resolution and appears designed by both parties to have none. The Hakari are matriarchally governed, with leadership authority tracing through female lineage. Their conflict with the Jaulaus has historical roots that predate outside contact and has been consistently resistant to outside mediation, possibly because both sides have internal factions that benefit from the conflict continuing. A phenomenon that complicates Hakari politics considerably is the diaspora inheritance problem: Hakari members living in Alliance Space regularly inherit clan leadership positions in communities they have never visited, acquiring cultural authority over people they have never met in a conflict they have only read about. Alliance mediators have documented this pattern frequently enough to treat it as a structural feature rather than an anomaly.
known_for: One of two native power structures on Mangara, in sustained civil war
Matriarchal governance structure
Consistent resistance to outside mediation
Diaspora leadership inheritance as a documented structural problem
No influence or operations outside the Mangara system
factions.legal_standing: Recognised indigenous government under Alliance Mangara protocol

factions.name: Jaulaus Tribal Councils
factions.desc: The Jaulaus Tribal Councils are the second native political structure on Mangara, tribally organised with council-based governance, and in sustained conflict with the Hakari Clans for longer than outside observers have been recording Mangaran history, which is itself a considerable length of time. The conflict is self-sustaining in the way that conflicts tend to be when both sides have internal factions that benefit commercially and politically from its continuation. Alliance intelligence has noted that announced ceasefires between the Hakari and Jaulaus have historically served as reliable advance indicators of significant escalation, and has incorporated this into its standard assessment models as an established pattern rather than a coincidence.
known_for: One of two native power structures on Mangara, in sustained civil war
Tribal council governance structure
Internal ceasefire-undermining factions documented across multiple decades
No influence or operations outside the Mangara system
Alliance intelligence classification of their ceasefires as escalation precursors
factions.legal_standing: Recognised indigenous government under Alliance Mangara protocol

factions.name: Lansing Corp
factions.hq: Undisclosed, believed Freeland or eastern Alliance Space
factions.desc: Lansing Corp produces the finest ships in the galaxy, and this has never once translated into commercial dominance, which is either a profound irony or a reasonable consequence of pricing that makes Arms Corp look accessible. The problem is that Lansing ships exceed every specification by margins that raise genuine questions about whether the excess is operationally useful. A Lansing vessel will perform well beyond what any buyer actually requires. The engineering is exceptional. The price reflects the engineering in full, with interest. The market for ships that cost significantly more than equivalent vessels from practical manufacturers and do things no buyer will ever need is small, but that market is committed, and Lansing has survived on its commitment for generations. Voran Industries' failed attempt to compete with Lansing in the aerospace market is a well-known cautionary case study that Lansing's current leadership still finds faintly amusing.
known_for: Ships that exceed all specifications by significant margins
The most collected vessels in the galaxy, a Lansing ship is a significant acquisition
Drove Voran Industries out of the aerospace market entirely
No ventures outside shipbuilding, Lansing does one thing
Engineering reputation that is universally acknowledged even by competitors who cannot afford to stock them
factions.legal_standing: Fully legal

factions.name: Solistar Mineral Corporation
factions.desc: Solistar is the largest asteroid mining corporation in the galaxy, which is a business that rewards scale ruthlessly and punishes everyone else. Its operations span the major asteroid belts within Alliance Space and extend into frontier zones where extraction rights were established ahead of formal settlement, a practice that is technically legal and practically unstoppable once the extraction infrastructure is already in place. The business model is straightforward: find the ore, extract it, ship it, sell it. Solistar does this at a scale and efficiency that has eliminated most independent asteroid mining competition within Alliance Space, not through malice but through the simple mathematics of operating costs. Its relationship with the Zegitor Trade Guild is close and commercially significant, and its supply contracts with Arms Corp manufacturing on Ishtar represent one of the most important bilateral commercial relationships in the Alliance economy, which is to say that both organisations would notice immediately if the other ceased to exist.
known_for: Largest asteroid mining operation in the galaxy
Dominant market position within Alliance Space extraction zones
Major supplier to Arms Corp manufacturing on Ishtar
Close commercial relationship with Zegitor Trade Guild
Frontier zone operations ahead of formal settlement, extraction rights established early
factions.legal_standing: Fully legal; Alliance extraction licensing

factions.name: Skalan Order
factions.hq: Unknown, believed to be outside Alliance Space in ungoverned territory
presence: Safe houses in Haven Space and frontier worlds
factions.desc: The Skalan Order is the organised remnant of Skalan loyalists who survived the genetic editing that destroyed their race's future. The Patriark's decision to apply the Skalan gene-edit, never officially characterised as punishment, containment, or policy, and presumably characterised as nothing at all if you ask the Patriark's communications office, ended the Skalan as a viable self-sustaining population. The Order exists to ensure this is not forgotten and to pursue the long-term goal of making those responsible answer for it in some form, at some point, on a timeline that most institutions find unsettling because they cannot plan against it. Its methods are not public. Its membership is not public. It makes no public statements and claims no actions. The patience it has demonstrated is the kind that comes from having genuinely nothing to lose by waiting.
known_for: Skalan loyalists organised around the goal of Patriark accountability
The Skalan gene-edit, the defining historical grievance
Operational secrecy, no public statements, no claimed actions
Patient long-term operation across timescales most institutions do not plan for
Cells throughout Alliance Space; haven in ungoverned space
factions.legal_standing: Illegal throughout Alliance Space; Patriark-designated terrorist organisation

factions.name: Assassin Guild
presence: Galactic, operates in all major regions
factions.desc: The Assassin Guild is exactly what the name describes, which in a galaxy full of organisations with deliberately misleading names is almost disorienting. Two distinctions separate it from every imitation: it operates at genuinely galactic scale, and it takes contracts that other organisations decline on grounds of difficulty, political sensitivity, or basic self-preservation. The Guild will take any contract. The price reflects difficulty, risk, and political complexity, and some contracts are priced at levels where accepting them is a statement of intent rather than a commercial transaction. The Guild's internal structure is unknown. Its membership is unknown. How contracts reach it is understood in criminal circles but not publicly documented. The only publicly observable data point is its record of completion, which is the entire reason it exists and the entire basis of its reputation.
known_for: Contract killing at galactic scale
Takes any contract regardless of difficulty or political sensitivity
Pricing that reflects difficulty, risk, and political complexity in full
Operational secrecy, structure, membership, and contact methods not publicly known
A completion record that is its primary commercial reputation
factions.legal_standing: Illegal in all known jurisdictions

factions.name: Skav'nauts
factions.hq: No fixed headquarters, distributed throughout Alliance Space
factions.desc: The Skav'nauts are organised criminal gangs operating throughout Alliance Space who have built a distinctive cultural identity around their crimes: they collect proof of what they have done and wear it. Trophies, documentation, and evidence of corporate theft are displayed as clothing, insignia, and status markers, which makes identification by law enforcement straightforward and is presumably a feature rather than an oversight. The Skav'nauts target corporations specifically; individuals are not the primary target and civilian collateral is actively avoided, a policy discipline that has given them a romanticised reputation in communities that view corporate property crime as something between sport and public service. Their actual behaviour is more complicated than the reputation, but the reputation is the one that has stuck. Alliance law enforcement classifies them as a significant organised crime concern, which is accurate, and notes that the public sympathy problem makes prosecution politically awkward in certain jurisdictions.
known_for: Crimes against corporate targets, corporations are the explicit focus
Wearing proof of crimes as status symbols and clothing insignia
A distributed gang network with consistent cultural identity across all Alliance sectors
A romanticised reputation among some communities that views them as anti-corporate
Alliance law enforcement priority target
factions.legal_standing: Illegal throughout Alliance Space

factions.name: Wastelanders
factions.hq: No fixed headquarters, mobile throughout frontier and Alliance worlds
factions.desc: The Wastelanders are the galaxy's practical distribution network for goods that need to move without documentation, a service that turns out to have substantial commercial demand from clients who technically do not exist in any official supply chain record. Loosely organised in mobile gang structures, they operate vehicles, ships, and convoys across inhabited and frontier worlds alike. They are not primarily violent; their commercial model depends on deliveries completing, and violence is bad for completion rates. They do operate in contested and ungoverned space as a matter of course, and they are equipped for the realities of those environments without being defined by them. The Wastelanders handle a significant fraction of frontier distribution that no licensed carrier will service, which makes them indispensable to frontier economies that Alliance logistics networks have never adequately reached. Finding them is less difficult than it sounds. They are in most transit environments. You just need to know which questions to ask.
known_for: Frontier and ungoverned space distribution, goods that need to move without paperwork
Mobile gang organisation, no fixed base
Non-violent as a commercial preference; equipped for frontier realities
Present in most transit environments throughout Alliance and frontier space
The practical option for distribution that legitimate carriers will not handle
factions.legal_standing: Illegal; enforcement priority varies by jurisdiction and available resources

factions.name: Seto Syndicate
factions.desc: The Seto Syndicate is the largest of the Sirius crime families and the most persuasive argument that organised crime and organised business are the same operation with different filing systems. Where most criminal outfits depend on loyalty, intimidation, and whoever currently controls the largest weapon, the Syndicate runs on defined planning horizons, operational divisions with clear remits, succession planning, and the kind of institutional memory that most legitimate corporations spend money trying to build and never quite manage. Financial operations, illegal logistics, protection arrangements, political influence, and contract services run simultaneously across multiple systems. The Sirius families collectively represent the most significant criminal infrastructure in Alliance Space. The Seto Syndicate is the largest and oldest among them, which is either impressive or deeply alarming depending entirely on whether you are a client or a creditor.
known_for: Largest single organised crime operation in Alliance Space
Sirius-based with genuinely galactic reach across all operational categories
Corporate structure with planning horizons most businesses cannot match
The dominant power among the Sirius crime families
Political and financial reach extending deep into institutions that are supposed to stop them
factions.legal_standing: Illegal; Alliance intelligence priority target

factions.name: Tanaka Syndicate
presence: Alliance Space, frontier and border regions
factions.desc: The Tanaka Syndicate is the second significant crime family operating out of Sirius, handling the local affairs the Seto Syndicate considers beneath its operational scale. Where Seto runs a galaxy-spanning corporate structure, Tanaka keeps things local and personal. Protection, local distribution, workforce arrangements of the involuntary variety, and the kind of municipal contract work that functions best when the counterparty either does not read the fine print or has concluded that raising objections would be inadvisable. Allegations of ties to the Alliance itself have circulated for years, alongside persistent claims of financial backing from Yamato Corporation, which has denied everything with the practised ease of an organisation that has been denying things for centuries and has never once been made to stop. Whether Yamato is funding a local crime operation or merely maintaining a commercially convenient relationship with one is, legally speaking, a distinction of considerable importance that nobody in a position to investigate seems motivated to pursue.
known_for: Dominant in local Sirius criminal affairs below the Seto Syndicate's operational scale
Alleged Alliance ties, unconfirmed and apparently uninvestigated
Suspected Yamato Corporation financial backing, denied by all parties
Local enforcement of the kind that does not involve filing paperwork
The practical infrastructure of Sirius crime for anyone who cannot afford Seto rates
factions.legal_standing: Illegal; investigation status unclear given alleged institutional ties

factions.name: Nerulian Pirate Fleet
factions.hq: San-Tien, believed largest concentration; rumoured Sirius asteroid base
factions.desc: The largest organised pirate fleet in the known galaxy is Nerulian-crewed and operates primarily out of San-Tien. The fleet is also the most convincing argument available that Kintech's claimed independence from San-Tien is not accurate: the operational overlap between Kintech equipment and Nerulian pirate vessels is noted in every serious intelligence assessment of the region, and has been noted consistently enough that not drawing the obvious conclusion requires a specific effort of will. There is additionally a persistent and widely-credited rumour of a major pirate base somewhere in the asteroid belt near the Sirius system, a staging point for operations that reach well into Alliance Space. The rumour is old enough and consistent enough across independent sources that most intelligence analysts treat it as probable. The base, if it exists, has not been found, which is either a tribute to its concealment or a commentary on how hard anyone is looking.
known_for: Largest organised pirate fleet in the known galaxy
Predominantly Nerulian crews operating from San-Tien
Equipment overlap with Kintech products, basis for ongoing intelligence assessment of the connection
The Sirius asteroid base rumour, persistent, widely credited, never confirmed
Operational range that reaches well into Alliance border systems
factions.legal_standing: Illegal throughout all Alliance and affiliated jurisdictions
